title: Get legal advice on satire before launch
description: One conversation with a lawyer about labelling, public figures, invented quotations, generated images, election-period rules on synthetic political content, and wholly fictional people and agencies: whether a quick web search of the name is enough to keep a fictional person from matching a real private person, and false light and defamation exposure for invented claims about real people.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Added 2026-11-15 (decision 24): the satire label is now ONE line in the page furniture, a slim footer fixed to the bottom of every page, pointing at the name; starting wording 'It's called THE HALLUCINATOR. None of this happened.' Please cover: the wording, whether one line is enough, placement (fixed footer, visible before a piece is read, survives a share preview), and whether the machine-readable markers (Markdown metadata, feed, structured data, llms.txt, share preview) are enough. Pieces carry no disclaimer paragraph.
